correctness.rationale: For generic hyperplane H separating K of the m simplex vertices, each section vertex is a crossed edge and exactly V=K(m-K). Independently verified direct crossed-edge enumeration for synthetic finite samples. A Gaussian vector with centered radius R and order statistics gives the correctly width-tilted Crofton law E[(1/R)int f(K(s)(m-K(s))) ds]/E(W/R), not uniform normal plus uniform offset. Its exact expectation is binom(m,2) E|Z1-Z2|/E range=binom(m,2)/(sqrt(pi) mu_m). Gaussian range endpoints at ±sqrt(2log m), concentration R/sqrt(m)->1 and width tilt in L1 yield a limiting uniform offset U in [-1,1]. Mills tail and binomial concentration imply log V/log m -> 2-U^2; for fixed 0<a<1/4, empirical central quantiles give an interval of length 2q_a+o_L2(1), and ratio to Gaussian range proves sqrt(2 log m) Pr[V>=a m^2]->q_a and the conditional marked law. No inference of infinite asymptotics from simulations.
